item.title: Re: An atavistic humanoid + a mysterious organization
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the critique! I did pass the 400 word count, but luckily Zyn fixed it for me.

+ Answers and reaction
- close
  • As for your first question: Yes, I intended on having humans in the past have this ability. There are a lot of stories about people with psychic powers, and some claim to posses it this day. The idea was that it was a rare mutation, that occurred in the past. That it wasn't some sort of superpower, but more like an reflex/instinctive reaction. It could for example be triggered by strong emotions. The thing is that those people either died at a young age because of the effects of the mutation, went insane, or got killed by other humans who thought they were dangerous. It wasn't beneficial for them.
  • About the IQ, what you are describing (not mathematically intelligent, but better in things that were useful around that time) is what I meant. Thank you for correcting me.
  • Evolution is (mostly) positive for the survival of the concerning organism's genes, right?
  • Negative in the current environment I meant. I do not think one of our ancestors would go good with today's environment.
  • So….. found remains of one of the ''psychic cavemen''. Are you suggesting that that is a better option?
  • Last but not least: about Latin. I was wondering what language the organization would be speaking, and since it is kind off a cult who wants to bring back ancient creatures trough science I figured that Latin would be fitting. The earliest version of the organization was around the 16th century, at the time of the renaissance (the time period where people were really inspired by the ancient cultures and the time period where almost all of the humanists/scientists wrote their papers in Latin). Wouldn't it make sense for the organization to have Latin as their spoken/taught language?

PS: I just tried to describe my idea in a sentence and ''An organization determined to recreate ancient mythological creatures creates a psychic caveman with trust issues'' doesn't sound as good as it sounded before. So allow me to ask you a question: is the no greenlight a ''you need to improve this idea''-no greenlight or a ''you could better start working on something else''-no greenlight?

item.title: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Hey CogWheel1950: two things.

First: please don't reply to yourself like this; if you want to add additional context etc., please edit it into the original post instead of making a new comment.

Secondly: per the Draft Forum's policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies, authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not an official critter here, but I can still read and give opinions.
So, I mostly agree with Grigori above. The idea is really cool, I personally love this kind of 'meta' stuff. But I would also recommend cutting out the anomalous weapon bit. I don't think the possession is a problem myself, it makes sense as a way for a fictional character to 'anchor' itself to our reality; but I think the anomalous weapons bit would simply make it look as though you're making it be more dangerous than it needs to be.
Not everything needs to be able to destroy a plane to be interesting.

This aside, I believe, another interesting concept you could explore instead- if you think the personal woes of Sir Reginald coming to terms with not being "real" are not enough- is how they got here at all, if that is still an active phenomenon/it can spread to other media, and what that means for whatever work Reginald is from originally.
Just a bunch of ideas, you're free to completely disregard them if you don't feel they're interesting enough for you.

Overall though, I really like this! Definitely gonna be reading it once it's written out as a draft and hopefully as a real Object!

I like this - an article devoted to pure collaborative worldbuilding, while controversial, is something I personally find interesting. But, as an avid world builder, I have some criticism to give.

+ Show
- hide

The Chitin Sea
Source of the River Tock… Immeasurably large biomass

This breaks one of the most important rules of worldbuilding 'rivers don't flow upwards.' As it is never specified that the river tock flows in reverse, or that the Chitan is built on higher ground than the rest of corbenic, so I'm gonna say that this river doesn't really make sense. It would probably be better to change this to something like:

The Chitin Sea
Found by following the Right Moon from the Great Desert, Valley of the Striders or following the River Tock to its mouth. Immeasurably large biomass…

Furthermore:

which is above the cloud layer and has not yet been observed, is said to contain the castle of SCP-PC-007

Is this cloud layer constant? If so, that should probably be specified.

Otherwise, I would love to see more of the culture of Corbenics inhabitants. At the moment we have some information on the structure of corbenic, but I'd love to see how the citizens of corbenic act, maybe in the form of 'essays' (maybe similar to those in SCP-4935 and SCP-5005) by project Galahad members based on testimonies from the Omega-16 group. But that's just my opinion. +1 anyway.

item.title: Re: The Normality
item.content:encoded:
Hi.
I've read your crit and I wanted to clear some things.
Firstly, I wasn't aware of the Djoric-Dmatix Proposal and its similarity to my idea until now. Thank you for that.
Secondly, while your concern about them being similar are true, I think they are different in essence.
1.) The Djoric-Dmatix Proposal, or the thirty-six, are somewhat aware of what they are capable of, and are part of something huge. However, the normality is just an average person, who lives an average life not knowing what he is and what he could do, and with no part of something grandiose.

2.) The normality does not influence anomalies over a large area, just that which is under his observation or could potentially affect his normal life. This shows that if he was left alone, he would not have affected the foundation or anything at all, and even now, with proper precaution, could be controlled, unlike the thirty-six

3.) The Thirty-Six are contained because they possess a risk of generating large amounts of anomaly upon death, and affecting the entire world. The normality is observed for a different reason, that is, his power to bring equilibrium could wipe out the foundation's existence without actually ending the world, not for threatening reality as we now know it. In other words, the normality is given SCP status not because he is anomalous, but rather because he is normal, a bit too much.

I am sure that you will have more concerns. If so, please do not hesitate to give me your feedback
Thank you

item.title: Re: Any suggestion for my first SCP? Feel free to comment
item.content:encoded:
Hello there, hope you are having a pleasant day. I have checked your SCP and it has mistakes, I will tell you some:
- You cant resign the object class after it breaches containment since the object classes are based on 1. Threat and 2. Percentage of breaching containment. For example, not every safe object class SCP is harmless it just means they are easy to contain.
- You are just talking about the background of the SCPs and not of actual SCPs aka mannequins so the audience can't tell you exactly what you are missing and what you are doing right.
- You should format your article that it's 2m x 2m x 2m meters for example containment since you are containing them in cubes, not flat squares.
- And the last one the description is too short, you barely explain their ability and their looks so that has to be longer.

I wish you a pleasant day and good luck with writing.

item.title: Re: The Spire - needs greenlights
item.content:encoded:
This idea feels…incredibly complex but without paying it off in an interesting way. Like, you have a spire with a tonne of random properties that are all like, kinda related and it might be fine if you did something interesting with it, but you…don't? The like, list of things that can cause a teleportation event in particular feels, complex instead of interesting: my general advice is to strip an anomaly down to the fewest moving parts it needs so you can focus on the interesting bits instead of producing a tonne of rules about how it works.

I think that's my bigger issue to be honest: the discovery section is fine but it feels like something you'd include as a quick nod to how it was found over the meat of the article, and the only other planned thing is 'test logs' but I don't really have a feel for what they actually like…involve?

I guess my top advice here is that you're trying to write an interesting short story, not a cool weird thing to include in a ttrpg; the way the the foundation interacts with this and what happens with it is going to be the key that makes this work.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: The Spire - needs greenlights

It is a real shame this has not received more attention. +9, and all the upvotes by noobies? Not to devalue the votes of noobies, but that is a real shame! To be fair, not much happens in this tale. It's so simple I hesitate to call it a "story", and I think you realized this and tried to rush in a kind of moral to it at the end. But. The prose was pretty good, the dialogue was enjoyable, the anomaly (even though it wasn't your own) was well-described and intriguing and gross. This definitely feels like the beginning of a longer story, but… yeah, what can I say, I liked it. +1 even if it doesn't go anywhere.

item.title: Re: What is Love?
item.content:encoded:
The original intent for the story was that I was going to leave it open-ended; the beginning essentially takes real-world recent history and views it through a fantastic lens. The idea was that the stalemate is still ongoing but appears to be losing effectiveness as time progresses (utilizing events such as Japan's birthrate reaching its lowest recorded number last year and America's marriage rates reaching a record low the year before as evidence).

My concern with this is that the open-ended nature here feels unsatisfying: the truce slowly falling apart feels…like a fine progression but I think it'd feel like it was missing closure if we didn't see how it all ended?

I also have some concerns about the progression through this: it feels…perhaps too loose? Like, in the sense that, I don't really have a clear idea of what the in article discussion is as the effectiveness is lost or like, what stance the various members of the stalemate are taking or anything.

Having tales building off this isn't a terrible idea but it feels…perhaps like they might feel stronger if included in the SCP?

You're going to have to give someone a lot more detail here before they can tell whether this idea is interesting: remember, you have 400 words to use to explain this.

Hermit crabs that do weird things.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for critique
– hide block

Small items may be offered as 'tribute' to prevent the doll's nature from taking important concepts/people.

What do you mean by 'taking' here? Is this like…a semantic hazard which might take the meaning of 'freedom' so no-one understands what it means anymore? Or is this more a small scale thing where it might take the concept of freedom which allows it to be free/to be interpreted as free?

To remain generally inert, the item must receive a tribute every 2-3 days.

I'm, generally not a fan of SCPs that like, force the Foundation to interact with them in this way; it's generally more interesting (at least to me) if they willingly choose to do something because then it opens you up to asking the question 'why did they choose to do this'.

This doll embodies Otaku obsession culture and gatekeeping culture as satire, giving a supernatural explanation for such phenomena.

As a satire, this feels…off? It doesn't so much satirise the phenomenon as just, repeat it verbatim but with a supernatural cause. This isn't necessarily an issue alone though.

The core of my concern with this proposal is that we have this interesting start to the story: the discovery of the anomaly, the identification of the otaku, the thing coming into foundation contact; but I don't know where all these individual parts go: what do you do with them all? How do you explore the idea of obsessive culture and otaku-ness and gatekeeping in this? What conclusions do you draw about it? Where do the interviews and the found footage take this narratively?

I have some concerns about the compulsive nature of this, it feels to me that the doll somehow inspiring the creation of otakus without forcing people to become them would be more interesting: it'd really let you like, explore why some people become so obsessive.

item.title: Re: A problem with alot of scp articles.
item.content:encoded:
They aren't actual scientific reports, they're short stories. We're a creative writing website. People will overlook some inaccuracies or a bit of casual language if the story is good enough, especially given that relatively few of the people on the site are actual scientists.

(Also, censorship makes sense of a clandestine organisation, but more importantly when done well it can serve a narrative purpose.)

Edit: Also, draft reviewers? 1) Generally very well versed in clinical tone despite most being non-scientists, 2) are doing difficult time-consuming work for free, 3) are often addressing much larger writing problems, and 4) have no control over what authors actually post.

This feels thin, I think you need to develop your narrative more. What is the stakes? Why does the Foundation need to make a whole site around this one thing?

There aren't any characters, there's very little plot mentioned, and I don't see any thematic elements that you want to discuss.

What makes you interested in this? What do you want the reader to take away from it? How will your story be told? As this, as it stands, is not even a monster manual entry… as it has very little substantive details.

item.title: Re: Memetic Instruction Pamphlets
item.content:encoded:
The whole "this anomaly makes you do bad things to other people" is so played out that I would be unlikely to find it particularly interesting. More so the whole "hidden group that knows more than the foundation and will be watching" brand new GoI.

I think at its core, this concept proposal shows that you know how to tell a story as the investigation sounds somewhat compelling but the core anomaly is sorta cliche…

I'd suggest going back to the drawing board as to the actual anomaly, because this just covers tropes that are too frequently leaned on in my opinion.

item.title: Re: SCP-5640 The Stomach IDEA looking for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
I agree with Cybersqyd's perspective below… I advised tying the anomaly to the political story, but then you've gone and sorta used this political story as just background for a weird thing

I'm much less interested in a story about something some horrible government used to silence dissidents that is really just about the Foundation studying something… I think this would be better served with less focus on the Foundation and more on the horrors of the anomaly.

If this is about disappeared folks, that's a heavy narrative theme right there… don't abandon it to focus on testing with cows. The testing wouldn't be nearly as engaging as a discussion of how this government used something so horrible to enact its disappearances.

Finally… as Sqyd said below, because this is a real situation where real people died and were vanished by a government, you have to be careful. You don't want to make this just an entertaining story… because you're talking about a great horror perpetrated in real life. So I would suggest focusing in on that, and using the article to discuss it in a way that is meaningful.

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the feedback. Some responses below.

+ Collapsed for brevity
- Close

If something was incorporeal in the core and then became corporeal, why would the core collapse?

It isn't simply more mass being added to the core, it is part of the core being replaced with the incorporeal objects, which are far less dense, allowing large amounts of additional matter to be pushed into the core in a large surge. it should also be noted that due to the nature of several types of intangibility there are several intangible corpse in a single place being expelled from each other while becoming corporeal, potentially causing large seismic disruptions due to the movement of large amounts of mass. As for the 'disastrous' aspect, that is what is being implied to happen in the scenario discussed at the end.

Don't do this, don't redact the size. It doesn't serve anything, do some research and figure out what sorta size you want to imply and just say it. Would be more impactful.

Fair enough, but what more impact would a unit of measure have? I am of the opinion that a well placed redaction can emphasize the horror of an article. To anyone who isn't familiar with the size of a human body or the size of the earths core a definitive amount I feel a definitive amount would lessen the impact. That being said, I may just blackbox the exact volume with a large amount of digits.

More of concern is the lack of narrative. There isn't an arc to this, its merely discussing the description of an anomaly. What is it you want to say with this article? What do you want the readers to take away from it? We can't really know what the people are going through as they sink to the center of the earth… so where is the human aspect of this anomaly?

You are correct in there not being a central narrative but for an anomaly of this type, there can't really be one, as it isn't the result of one central anomaly. The human aspect of this article comes in the form of the individual stories of the people down there, implied through their descriptions. Furthermore, due to the nature of certain types of intangibility some of the people are still alive and fully aware of their situation. Given that I am planning on having at least one of the people as a ghost, the foundation may be able to conduct an interview with them via use of a séance. Ending the article with the potential of disaster is meant to convey how this is truly a lose-lose situation, with them being stuck, us being doomed and neither party being able to do anything about it.

item.title: Re: Around the world
item.content:encoded:
I don't mean to be harsh but the phrasing in the elevator pitch has me very confused. How would one look at a compas from 200 meters away? How big is this compass?

moreover, it feels a bit like a run of the mill "other dimension" exploration… I think what you need to do is add some character to both the other dimension and those who are going to be trapped there. What sort of story do you wanna play with here? is there a theme you're working with (other than, alternate universes)?

Keep in mind, the sky is the limit with anomalies and alternative universes… so what can you do to make this one stand out?

Additionally I would simplify the logic of how people are transported to this other dimension. Also You don't need to designate an observer as part of the SCP unless they're somehow changed. You could just say "individuals observing SCP-XXXX"
